Agreed next steps: send pricing, security docs, and run a 2-week pilot to validate throughput and latency under Clarion traffic.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Kim (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Clarion CTO), Aaron Lee (Clarion Lead ML Eng), Priya Singh (Clarion Security), Evan Carter (Clarion DevOps)

[00:00:05] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Sofia, AE at Redwood, and with me are Daniel and Lena from our SE team. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Maya: Good thanks, excited to see how you handle rate limits. we've had some outages with our current provider when our mobile app spikes.
[00:00:00] Aaron: yeah hi, Aaron here - mostly interested in quotas per product and per-tenant isolation.
[00:00:22] Daniel: Great, today we'll focus on org and project keys, how rate-limits and quotas map to them, console walk-through and example API calls. we'll also show how you can set per-route limits and burst capacity.
[00:00:35] Lena: quick note, some of the transcription may call it K V cash (laughs) - it's KV cache.
[00:00:40] Priya: also I'm Priya from security, i'll be asking about audit logs, KMS, and data retention.

--- Demo start ---
[00:01:10] Daniel: i'm sharing my screen. first slide is the org vs project model - an org is your company, projects map to products or teams. org-level defaults apply to all projects, and projects can have overrides. so for Clarion you could have a global token-per-minute quota for the org and then higher limits for the mobile-project and stricter limits for internal-admin project.
[00:01:45] Maya: does that translate to separate billing buckets?
[00:01:50] Sofia: yes you can bill at org level and break down usage by project for chargeback. we also support project-level billing exports.
[00:02:05] Daniel: switching to the console - here's the rate-limits page. you can create a policy, select scope (org or project), set RPS and token-based quotas, and define burst windows.
[00:02:20] [00:02:25] (transcription glitch: "burst windows" heard as "bust windows")
[00:02:30] Lena: live demo: creating a policy - name it "mobile-prod-burst", scope: project:mobile, rate limit: 200 requests per minute, burst: 500 tokens for 30s window. you can also add per-route overrides, e.g., /chat/completions has a separate quota.
[00:02:55] Aaron: in our case, we need per-customer tenant isolation inside a project. can we do per-customer limits?
[00:03:05] Daniel: good question. you can implement sub-quotas using project keys - create keys per customer and attach a sub-quota. it's not a separate project but keys can carry their own limits and tags for reporting.
[00:03:20] Maya: is that enforced at the edge or in the runtime?
[00:03:25] Daniel: edge enforcement - we rate-limit at the request gateway before it hits the runtime to avoid wasted compute. there are also runtime guards to protect KV cache and model instances.
[00:03:40] Priya: how are these keys issued? and can they rotate automatically?
[00:03:45] Lena: keys are issued from the org console, you can create org-scoped keys or project-scoped keys. rotation can be automated via our API; we also support short-lived keys integrated with your identity provider.
[00:03:58] Evan: for on-prem or VPC, do the same controls apply?
[00:04:03] Daniel: yes, same abstractions for Private; however, some cloud-managed features like automatic key rotation via our control plane require connectivity - for air-gapped we provide a key management guide and HSM/KMS integration instructions.

[00:04:30] [00:04:40] (crosstalk)
[00:04:45] Sofia: quick pause - Priya, any immediate red flags from a security standpoint?
[00:04:50] Priya: SOC2 and ISO are checkboxes, but i need to see audit log retention details and whether keys can be scoped by role. RBAC needs to be granular - ability to create keys but restrict which teams can apply quota overrides.
[00:05:10] Daniel: we have role-based policies - admin, billing, ops, read-only; you can attach policies to users via SSO (SAML/OIDC). audit logs capture key creation, quota changes, and API calls with project/key metadata. retention is configurable depending on your plan.
[00:05:30] Aaron: what's the latency impact of org-level routing and quotas?
[00:05:35] Daniel: negligible - the gateway is optimized; typical added latency is 2-5ms for policy checks. we use a distributed token bucket implementation. for high-throughput, you can use a cached token layer at the edge which reduces checks for bursty loads.

[00:06:00] Daniel: demo - API example: curl to /v1/requests with Authorization: Bearer PROJECT_KEY. header x-org-id optional for org-level routing. let me paste a sample in chat.
[00:06:15] (Daniel pastes curl, some words mis-transcribed: "curl with bearer proj key" -> "curl with bearer prog key")
[00:06:30] Lena: example response on quota-exceeded: 429 with Retry-After and JSON body showing "quota_id", "remaining", "reset_in_seconds" for programmatic handling.
[00:06:45] Maya: can we set alerts when a project hits 80% of quota?
[00:06:50] Sofia: yes - percent-based alerts, Slack/webhook/email. you can also set automatic fallback policies: if primary model rate limit is reached, route to a cheaper model variant or degrade gracefully.

[00:07:20] Aaron: about burst handling - if mobile app spikes, we need short bursts without long-term throttling. how do you prevent long tail throttles?
[00:07:28] Daniel: burst windows and token buckets handle that; also we have configurable cooldowns. for sustained spikes we recommend autoscaling with Dedicated capacity or routing to a lower-cost region.
[00:07:45] Maya: could you demo applying a per-route override?
[00:07:50] Daniel: sure - navigating to routes, selecting /chat/completions, adding override: 50 rps, burst 200 for 20s. saving - applies immediately. note: in console there's a simulator to test with sample traffic patterns.

[00:08:30] [00:08:40] (transcription: "simulator" -> "simulater")
[00:08:45] Lena: demo recording: running the simulator for 60s with a 1k qps spike - console shows dropped requests, suggestions to increase burst or add a canary autoscale rule. you can export the run as CSV for cost modeling.

[00:09:20] Priya: audit logs - are they tamper-evident?
[00:09:25] Daniel: logs are write-once and hashed; for Private we support pushing logs to your SIEM via secure forwarders. we also have signed event streams for compliance reviews.

[00:10:00] Aaron: do rate limits use tokens or characters? our billing is token-based.
[00:10:05] Sofia: quotas are token-based by default to match billing, but you can create request-count quotas for use-cases where tokens aren't primary.

[00:10:30] Evan: on the network side, do you support IP allowlists per key?
[00:10:35] Lena: yes, project keys can be restricted by IP, VPC egress ranges, or via JWTs issued from your IDP.

[00:11:00] Maya: what about per-route cost accounting? we need to allocate costs to product teams.
[00:11:05] Sofia: usage is tagged by project, route, and key; billing exports include these tags and per-token costs. you can integrate with your internal billing system via S3 export or direct API.

[00:11:35] Daniel: quick note on fallback routing - you can define policy that if qps exceeds X, route requests to cheaper model or to a cached response; this helps protect SLOs.

[00:12:00] (customer asks about benchmark)
[00:12:05] Aaron: we want to run a benchmark with our traffic profile - sequence lengths vary, some long context for patient summaries. will you run that on Dedicated?
[00:12:15] Daniel: we can run a pilot on Hosted first for quick results; if you need committed throughput we'll size Dedicated. for long context, we recommend specific kernel profiles and quantization to preserve latency.

[00:12:45] Sofia: i'm going to share pricing options soon, but pilot usually includes trial credits and a small Dedicated reservation if you want stable latency.

[00:13:00] Priya: data residency - some patient data can't leave certain regions. can we enforce region-level routing?
[00:13:07] Lena: yes, policies can be region-locked; requests with project keys will be routed to region endpoints. for Private/on-prem, data never leaves your VPC.

[00:13:30] [00:13:40] (brief silence)
[00:13:47] Maya: about team access - can we let product managers create keys but not change quotas?
[00:13:53] Daniel: yes - RBAC roles let you restrict quota editing to ops/admin roles. key creation can be scoped to 'creator' role without quota permissions.

[00:14:10] Aaron: any best-practices for multi-tenant limits?
[00:14:15] Sofia: yes - one is to issue keys per-customer and set soft-limits with alerts at 70/85/95% and hard-limits with automatic fallback to a lower-cost model. another is to shard heavy workloads into separate projects to avoid noisy neighbor effects. also tag keys for billing and retention rules.

[00:15:00] Daniel: demo - API timeouts and Retry-After examples. show client library behavior: when quota is hit, SDK automatically backs off respecting Retry-After header.

[00:15:30] Lena: note: some of our customers had misconfigured client retries that caused thundering herd during recovery; recommend jittered backoff.

[00:15:50] Priya: can we get a copy of your security handbook and SOC2 evidence?
[00:15:55] Sofia: yes, will send SOC2 summary and security pack. for deeper reviews we'll set up an NDA'd exchange.

[00:16:10] Maya: timeline - we want to pilot in early July, run for two weeks, then decide on Dedicated later in July.
[00:16:18] Sofia: that aligns with our standard POC flow. we'll propose pilot terms in the follow-up.

[00:16:30] (walkthrough continued - more console screens and Q&A, audio snippets omitted here for brevity)

[00:25:20] Daniel: quick demo of programmatic key creation via API - POST /v1/keys with {scope: project, quota: {tokens_per_min: 1000}}. response returns key id and masked key. remember to store securely.
[00:25:40] Aaron: can we bulk-create keys for customers?
[00:25:45] Lena: yes, there's a bulk API and CSV import tool in the console.

[00:26:10] Priya: about log retention costs - is long-term storage an add-on?
[00:26:15] Sofia: longer retention is an add-on in the hosted plan; with Private you can set retention to match your policies and host logs in your S3.

[00:27:00] Maya: what if a key is compromised - revocation process?
[00:27:05] Daniel: revoke via console or API, and you can rotate keys automatically. we also generate a timeline event in audit logs for revocation.

[00:27:25] Evan: network-level controls - is there a way to enforce that only requests signed by our JWTs can use a project key?
[00:27:32] Lena: yes you can require JWT assertion and map claims to project tenants; we validate signatures and TTL.

[00:28:00] Sofia: recap and next steps - we'll send pricing, security docs, demo recording, and a recommended pilot plan.
[00:28:10] Maya: thanks, can you include sample quotas you recommended?
[00:28:15] Daniel: yes - we'll include those in the follow-up e-mail; initial suggestion for mobile: org default 50k tokens/min, project mobile 100k tokens/min, per-customer keys with soft-limit 2k tokens/min.

[00:28:40] Maya: one last thing - do you integrate with our internal monitoring (Datadog)?
[00:28:45] Sofia: yes, metrics and traces export to Datadog, Prometheus, and you can send events to S3 or SIEM.

[00:29:00] Priya: ok i'm satisfied for now, will review security pack when you share.
[00:29:05] Aaron: thanks all, we'll get our traffic profile to you by end of week.

[00:29:20] Sofia: perfect - i'll follow up with an email summarizing these action items and attach the docs. thanks everyone.

[00:29:30] (call ends)

--- End transcript ---

Notes on transcription: Occasional mis-hearings (e.g., "K V cash" for KV cache, "prog key" for project key) and a few timestamp drift in the auto captions. The transcript captures the main demo flow: org/project model, keys with sub-quotas, per-route overrides, burst windows, RBAC, audit logs, region routing, and pilot next steps.
